investigation.title: Remote Agent Pod Scheduling Failure: Exhausted kata.peerpods.io/vm Capacity Across All 6 Nodes
investigation.summary: All three remote-agent checks (remote-agent-create, remote-agent-state, remote-agent-runtime) failed in production-api at 2026-07-09T01:01–01:08Z with an identical Kubernetes scheduling error: 0/6 nodes are available due to 2 nodes reporting Insufficient kata.peerpods.io/vm and 4 nodes not matching the pod's node affinity/selector. Because the pod never scheduled, the agent VM was never provisioned, and the eval runner could not collect any required evidence (orgId, agentId, vmIdPresent, remoteState), causing a complete contract validation failure.
investigation.rootCause: The Kubernetes cluster backing the remote-agent feature has exhausted the allocatable kata.peerpods.io/vm resource on the 2 nodes that carry that resource, and the remaining 4 nodes do not satisfy the pod's node affinity or node selector constraints. With no schedulable node and no preemption victims available, every remote-agent pod request times out unscheduled (~142–152 s), preventing VM creation and leaving all required eval evidence (orgId, agentId, vmIdPresent, remoteState) absent. This is an infrastructure capacity/scheduling failure localized to the remote-agent Kubernetes node pool, not an application code defect.

source-context.infra/evals/status/check-expectations.json:250-258: contract requires vmIdPresent=true and remoteState oneOf [running, idle, ready] — neither assertion can be evaluated when the pod never starts
possibleCauses: PRIMARY — kata.peerpods.io/vm resource exhaustion on the 2 eligible nodes: all allocatable VM slots are consumed by existing pods, leaving no capacity for new remote-agent pods. Preemption found no victims, indicating no lower-priority pods are present to evict.

SECONDARY — Node affinity/selector misconfiguration or drift: the 4 remaining nodes do not carry the kata.peerpods.io/vm extended resource or do not match the required node labels/taints, reducing the schedulable pool to only 2 nodes and amplifying the capacity problem.
TERTIARY — Cluster under-provisioning: the node pool size (6 nodes, only 2 with kata.peerpods.io/vm) may be insufficient for the concurrent remote-agent demand at the time of the eval run.

LOWER CONFIDENCE — A recent node or resource quota change that reduced available kata.peerpods.io/vm slots; no suspect changes are listed in sourceDiscovery.suspectChanges so this remains speculative.

investigation.title: Remote Agents: All Three Checks Failing Due to Exhausted kata.peerpods.io/vm Capacity on Kubernetes Cluster
investigation.summary: All three remote-agents eval checks (remote-agent-create, remote-agent-state, remote-agent-runtime) failed at 2026-07-09T01:03–01:08Z with an identical Kubernetes scheduler message: the 6-node production cluster has zero schedulable nodes for new kata peer-pod VMs — 2 nodes report insufficient kata.peerpods.io/vm capacity and 4 nodes do not match the pod's node affinity/selector. Because the agent pod could never be scheduled, the eval runner's createAgent call never returned a live agent, so no evidence (orgId, agentId, readyState, state) was ever written and the expected-output contract was fully violated.
investigation.rootCause: The Kubernetes cluster backing the remote-agents feature has exhausted its kata.peerpods.io/vm resource quota on the 2 nodes that carry that resource label. The remaining 4 nodes do not satisfy the pod's node affinity/selector, so preemption is also impossible. Every attempt to schedule a new remote-agent pod during this eval window was rejected by the scheduler after ~142–147 seconds, preventing agent creation and making all downstream state-polling and runtime checks unreachable. This is an infrastructure-layer capacity failure localized to the remote-agents Kubernetes node pool, not a code defect in the eval runner or the API service itself.

possibleCauses: kata.peerpods.io/vm resource quota exhausted on the 2 eligible nodes: concurrent or leaked remote-agent pods from prior eval runs or production workloads have consumed all available VM slots, leaving none for new probe pods. This is the strongest explanation given the explicit 'Insufficient kata.peerpods.io/vm' message in all three sibling check failures.

Node affinity/selector mismatch on 4 of 6 nodes: the pod spec requires a node label or taint that only 2 nodes carry, and those 2 are already at capacity. A recent node pool scaling event, node label change, or taint modification could have reduced the effective schedulable pool.

Cluster under-provisioned for concurrent eval load: if multiple eval runs or production workloads simultaneously request kata peer-pod VMs, the 2-node pool may be too small to absorb the burst, causing transient exhaustion during the eval window.
Leaked/zombie remote-agent pods holding kata.peerpods.io/vm slots: prior eval runs that did not clean up successfully may have left pods running and consuming VM quota, preventing new scheduling.

whatWouldDisproveThis: If kubectl or equivalent tooling shows kata.peerpods.io/vm capacity is available and unallocated on the eligible nodes at the time of the failure, the exhaustion hypothesis would be weakened and a different scheduling or API-layer cause would need to be investigated.

If the remote-agent-create check passes in a subsequent run while remote-agent-state still fails, the root cause would be localized to the state-polling logic rather than shared pod scheduling infrastructure.

If the 4 nodes with affinity/selector mismatches are shown to have recently had their labels or taints changed to match the pod spec, and the 2 kata-capable nodes have free capacity, the cause would shift to a node affinity configuration regression rather than resource exhaustion.

If no leaked or zombie pods are found consuming kata.peerpods.io/vm slots and the resource quota is shown to be genuinely too small for even a single new pod, the cause would be a cluster under-provisioning issue rather than quota exhaustion from leaked workloads.

If the eval runner's withCleanup or createAgent logic is shown to have a bug that causes it to emit the scheduler error message even when scheduling succeeds, the infrastructure diagnosis would be invalidated.

Add a leaked-pod detection eval that lists running remote-agent pods older than a configurable TTL and fails if any are found, catching cleanup failures before they exhaust node quota.

Add a node-affinity coverage eval that verifies at least N nodes satisfy the remote-agent pod's nodeAffinity/nodeSelector at the start of each eval run, alerting on pool shrinkage before it causes scheduling failures.

Add a sibling-correlation eval that automatically flags when all checks under a feature share the same scheduler error message, surfacing shared infrastructure dependency failures as a distinct signal from individual check regressions.

Because the pod never scheduled, no agent VM was created, no runtime response was produced, and all 5 required evidence fields (orgId, agentId, model, provider, message) are absent. This is an eval-observed infrastructure capacity or scheduling constraint failure localized to the remote-agents swarm cluster in the production-api environment; no user-traffic or incident signals are present in the supplied evidence.

investigations.title: Remote Agent Pod Scheduling Failure: Exhausted kata.peerpods.io/vm Capacity Across All 6 Nodes
investigations.summary: All three remote-agent checks (remote-agent-create, remote-agent-state, remote-agent-runtime) failed in production-api at 2026-07-09T01:01–01:08Z with an identical Kubernetes scheduling error: 0/6 nodes are available due to 2 nodes reporting Insufficient kata.peerpods.io/vm and 4 nodes not matching the pod's node affinity/selector. Because the pod never scheduled, the agent VM was never provisioned, and the eval runner could not collect any required evidence (orgId, agentId, vmIdPresent, remoteState), causing a complete contract validation failure.
investigations.rootCause: The Kubernetes cluster backing the remote-agent feature has exhausted the allocatable kata.peerpods.io/vm resource on the 2 nodes that carry that resource, and the remaining 4 nodes do not satisfy the pod's node affinity or node selector constraints. With no schedulable node and no preemption victims available, every remote-agent pod request times out unscheduled (~142–152 s), preventing VM creation and leaving all required eval evidence (orgId, agentId, vmIdPresent, remoteState) absent. This is an infrastructure capacity/scheduling failure localized to the remote-agent Kubernetes node pool, not an application code defect.

sibling.remote-agent-runtime: same scheduling error (142 s stuck), latencyMs=147626, endedAt=2026-07-09T01:08:36.196Z

source-context.infra/evals/status/check-expectations.json:250-258: contract requires vmIdPresent=true and remoteState oneOf [running, idle, ready] — neither assertion can be evaluated when the pod never starts
possibleCauses: PRIMARY — kata.peerpods.io/vm resource exhaustion on the 2 eligible nodes: all allocatable VM slots are consumed by existing pods, leaving no capacity for new remote-agent pods. Preemption found no victims, indicating no lower-priority pods are present to evict.

SECONDARY — Node affinity/selector misconfiguration or drift: the 4 remaining nodes do not carry the kata.peerpods.io/vm extended resource or do not match the required node labels/taints, reducing the schedulable pool to only 2 nodes and amplifying the capacity problem.
TERTIARY — Cluster under-provisioning: the node pool size (6 nodes, only 2 with kata.peerpods.io/vm) may be insufficient for the concurrent remote-agent demand at the time of the eval run.

LOWER CONFIDENCE — A recent node or resource quota change that reduced available kata.peerpods.io/vm slots; no suspect changes are listed in sourceDiscovery.suspectChanges so this remains speculative.

investigations.summary: All three remote-agents eval checks (remote-agent-create, remote-agent-state, remote-agent-runtime) failed at 2026-07-09T01:03–01:08Z with an identical Kubernetes scheduler message: the 6-node production cluster has zero schedulable nodes for new kata peer-pod VMs — 2 nodes report insufficient kata.peerpods.io/vm capacity and 4 nodes do not match the pod's node affinity/selector. Because the agent pod could never be scheduled, the eval runner's createAgent call never returned a live agent, so no evidence (orgId, agentId, readyState, state) was ever written and the expected-output contract was fully violated.
investigations.rootCause: The Kubernetes cluster backing the remote-agents feature has exhausted its kata.peerpods.io/vm resource quota on the 2 nodes that carry that resource label. The remaining 4 nodes do not satisfy the pod's node affinity/selector, so preemption is also impossible. Every attempt to schedule a new remote-agent pod during this eval window was rejected by the scheduler after ~142–147 seconds, preventing agent creation and making all downstream state-polling and runtime checks unreachable. This is an infrastructure-layer capacity failure localized to the remote-agents Kubernetes node pool, not a code defect in the eval runner or the API service itself.

possibleCauses: Primary — kata.peerpods.io/vm resource exhaustion on the 2 eligible swarm nodes: all available VM slots are consumed by existing pods, leaving no capacity for new eval agent pods. Supported directly by the scheduler message in failed-check.message and all three sibling failures.

Secondary — node affinity/selector misconfiguration or drift: the 4 remaining nodes do not satisfy the pod's affinity/selector rules, meaning only 2 nodes are even eligible, amplifying the impact of any capacity shortfall. Supported by the '4 node(s) didn't match Pod's node affinity/selector' clause in failed-check.message.

Tertiary — cluster-wide node count insufficient for the current workload: with only 6 nodes total, 2 eligible, and 0 preemption victims available, the cluster may be undersized for concurrent eval and production workloads. Supported by 'No preemption victims found' in failed-check.message.

Lower confidence — transient spike in concurrent remote agent workloads consuming all kata.peerpods.io/vm slots at the time of the eval run: the three sibling evals ran sequentially (01:03, 01:06, 01:08) and all failed, suggesting the condition persisted across the full eval window rather than being a momentary blip.

recommendedNextActions: Immediately check the kata.peerpods.io/vm resource allocation on the 2 eligible swarm nodes to determine whether slots are exhausted by long-running or leaked agent pods from prior eval runs or production workloads.

Review whether the withCleanup wrapper in run-status-probes.mjs (line 1916) is correctly terminating agent pods after each eval run; leaked pods from prior runs could be holding kata.peerpods.io/vm slots and causing progressive exhaustion.

Audit the node affinity/selector rules on the remote agent pod spec to determine whether the 4 non-matching nodes could be made eligible (e.g., by adding the required labels), which would increase the schedulable pool from 2 to up to 6 nodes.

If resource exhaustion is confirmed, consider increasing the kata.peerpods.io/vm capacity on the eligible nodes or expanding the number of nodes that carry this resource to reduce sensitivity to concurrent workloads.

Monitor the remote-agents feature degraded/outage thresholds: features.json lines 187–188 show degradedAfterFailures=1 and outageAfterFailures=2; with all three checks failing, the feature is at or past the outage threshold for the eval system.

whatWouldDisproveThis: If kubectl describe nodes showed available (unallocated) kata.peerpods.io/vm capacity on the 2 eligible nodes at the time of the eval run, resource exhaustion would be disproved and a different scheduling or API error would need to be identified.
If a re-run of the eval immediately after the failure succeeded and produced all 5 required evidence fields, the failure would be transient rather than a sustained capacity constraint.

If the remote-agent-runtime eval passed while remote-agent-create and remote-agent-state continued to fail, the root cause would be localized to a runtime-specific configuration rather than a shared pod scheduling constraint.

If the node affinity/selector rules on the pod spec were found to match more than 2 nodes, the '4 node(s) didn't match' clause would indicate a cluster node labeling drift rather than an intentional affinity constraint.

If user-traffic or incident signals showed remote agent provisioning succeeding for real users during the same window, the failure would be isolated to the eval probe's service account, namespace, or resource quota rather than a cluster-wide capacity issue.
followUpEvals: Add a pre-flight eval check that queries the kata.peerpods.io/vm allocatable vs. allocated counts on swarm nodes before attempting agent creation, surfacing capacity exhaustion as a distinct 'warn' status rather than a scheduling timeout failure.

Add an eval that verifies the number of nodes matching the remote agent pod's affinity/selector is above a minimum threshold (e.g., >= 2), catching node labeling drift before it reduces the schedulable pool.
Add a pod-cleanup verification eval that confirms no orphaned remote agent pods from prior eval runs are holding kata.peerpods.io/vm slots after the withCleanup phase completes.
Consider a canary eval that runs remote-agent-create with a reduced resource request to distinguish between affinity/selector mismatches and true resource exhaustion as separate failure modes.
